title: Chapter 37 — Sunset
paragraphs: The cabin, by the stern windows. Ahab sitting alone, gazing out.
I leave a white and troubled wake. Pale waters, paler cheeks, wherever I sail. The jealous waves swell sideways to swallow my track. Let them — but first I pass.

Yonder, at the ever-brimming goblet's rim, the warm waves blush like wine. The golden brow sinks into the blue. The diving sun — slowly descended from noon — goes down. My soul rises up! She tires of her endless climb. Is, then, the crown too heavy that I wear? This Iron Crown of Lombardy. Yet it is bright with many a gem. I, the wearer, cannot see its distant flashing — but I darkly feel that I wear something that dazzles and confounds. It is iron — that I know — not gold. It is cracked, too — I feel it. The jagged edge chafes me so, my brain seems to beat against the solid metal. Yes, a steel skull, mine — the kind that needs no helmet in the most brutal fight!

Dry heat upon my brow? Oh! There was a time when the sunrise nobly stirred me and the sunset soothed. No more. This lovely light — it doesn't light me. All beauty is agony to me, since I can never enjoy it. Gifted with the high perception, I lack the low, enjoying power. Damned — most subtly and most cruelly! Damned in the midst of Paradise! Good night — good night! (Waving his hand, he moves from the window.)

It was not so hard a task. I expected to find at least one man stubborn, but my one geared circle fits into all their various wheels, and they revolve. Or, if you prefer, like so many anthills of gunpowder, they all stand before me — and I am their match. Oh, how hard! That to set others ablaze, the match itself must burn away! What I have dared, I have willed. And what I have willed, I will do! They think me mad — Starbuck does. But I am demonic. I am madness gone mad! That wild madness which is only calm enough to comprehend itself! The prophecy said I would be dismembered — and yes! I lost this leg. I now prophesy that I will dismember my dismemberer. So let me be both prophet and fulfiller in one. That's more than you great gods ever were. I laugh at you and mock you, you cricket-players, you boxers, you deaf Burkes and blinded Bendigoes! I will not say as schoolboys say to bullies: pick on someone your own size, don't beat me! No — you've knocked me down, and I am back on my feet. But you have run and hidden. Come out from behind your barricades! I have no gun to reach you. Come, Ahab sends his compliments — come and see if you can turn me aside. Turn me? You cannot turn me — or else you turn yourselves! There, mankind has the advantage. Turn me? The path to my fixed purpose is laid with iron rails, and my soul is grooved to run on them. Over bottomless gorges, through the rifled hearts of mountains, under the beds of torrents, I rush without swerving! Nothing is an obstacle, nothing is a detour on the iron way!
